records.heading: config: site.ssl
comment: Turns https/http on or off when generating links

records.heading: config: site.secret
comment: IMPORTANT: After setting the secret, it should not be changed.
Be sure to create and store a backup in a secure offsite
location. Changing the secret can lead to unforeseen issues
like not being able to decrypt existing secrets.
See docs/runbooks/secret-rotation.md before touching it.

records.heading: config: site.secret_verifier_mode
comment: Boot-time SECRET verifier (QS-6). The app stores an HKDF-derived
verifier in the datastore and checks it on every boot, so a changed
SECRET (or a datastore from another install) is detected instead of
silently making existing secrets undecryptable.
warn    - log loudly on mismatch, keep booting (default)
enforce - refuse to boot on mismatch
off     - skip the check (escape hatch for multi-tenant datastores)

records.heading: config: site.interface.ui.enabled
comment: Controls whether the web interface is enabled
When false, only a basic explanation page is shown

records.heading: config: site.interface.ui.homepage.disabled_variant
comment: Deployment-wide default landing page for the CANONICAL site when the
homepage secret form is gated by auth (auth.required or mode=external).
One of: closed (quiet two-tagline, no CTA), minimal, or v1. Per-domain
config and the ?variant= URL override take precedence; blank uses the
frontend default (closed). Applies to the canonical site only —
custom domains use custom_disabled_variant below.

records.heading: config: site.interface.ui.homepage.custom_disabled_variant
comment: Deployment-wide default landing page for CUSTOM DOMAINS whose homepage
is private (homepage disabled, or incoming mode degraded at runtime).
Same values as disabled_variant (closed / minimal / v1). Kept separate
so the canonical and custom-domain defaults stay decoupled: a custom
domain does NOT inherit disabled_variant. Per-domain config
(homepage_config.disabled_homepage_variant) and the ?variant= URL
override take precedence; blank uses the frontend default (closed).

records.heading: config: site.interface.ui.homepage.public_links.recipient_intro
comment: URL the "What is this link?" affordance points at. When empty,
the affordance is hidden in the disabled-homepage view.

records.heading: config: site.interface.ui.header.enabled
comment: Control switch to enable/disable header customization

records.heading: config: site.interface.ui.header.logo.href
comment: Where the logo lockup links to. Unset uses '/'.

records.heading: config: site.interface.ui.header.logo.show_name

notes: three-state: nil when unset or blank

comment: Show the product name as a text mark next to the logo icon.
Unset (default): shown, unless a custom brand logo is configured
(custom logos usually embed their own wordmark). Set true/false
to force either way. The product name itself comes from
BRAND_PRODUCT_NAME and remains active in page titles, MFA labels,
and emails regardless of this knob.

records.heading: config: site.interface.ui.header.logo.prominent

notes: three-state: nil when unset or blank

comment: Render the logo at a larger size in the authenticated header.
Useful for rasterized brand assets (e.g. BRAND_LOGO_URL=/img/brand.png)
that need more visual presence alongside the org/domain switchers.
The default (unset/false) keeps the logo compact (40px) so context
switchers fit on the same row. When true, custom logos render at
80px in authenticated views. Unauthenticated views (branded
homepage / disabled page) always render the logo prominently.

records.heading: config: site.interface.ui.header.navigation.enabled
comment: Enable/disable header navigation entirely

records.heading: config: site.interface.ui.footer_links.enabled
comment: Global toggle to enable/disable all footer links

records.heading: config: site.interface.ui.footer_links.groups[0].name
comment: The "legal" group is a projection of site.legal above: each link's
URL resolves from there (normalize_legal in lib/onetime/config.rb),
and an entry whose URL is unset is dropped from the payload — no
placeholder, no dead link. Set the URLs via TERMS_URL, PRIVACY_URL,
DPA_URL, COOKIE_URL, AUP_URL, SECURITY_URL (or site.legal directly).

records.heading: config: site.interface.ui.footer_links.groups[1].links[0].url
comment: Replace with your documentation URL

records.heading: config: site.interface.ui.footer_links.groups[1].links[1].url
comment: Replace with your status page URL if you have one

records.heading: config: site.interface.ui.footer_links.groups[2].links[0].url
comment: Replace with your about page URL

records.heading: config: site.interface.ui.workspace_links.enabled
comment: Global toggle to enable/disable all footer links

records.heading: config: site.interface.ui.show_version
comment: Show or hide the version number in the workspace footer

records.heading: config: site.interface.api.guest_routes.enabled
comment: Global toggle - disables all guest routes when false

records.heading: config: site.interface.api.guest_routes.conceal
comment: Fine-grained controls (checked only when enabled=true)

records.heading: config: site.session.secret
comment: Session secret for HMAC signing. Falls back to site.secret if not set.

records.heading: config: site.session.expire_after
comment: Session lifetime in seconds (default: 24 hours)

records.heading: config: site.session.absolute_timeout
comment: Absolute session lifetime in seconds since sign-in, however active the
session is (default: 30 days). 0 disables the bound. See config.yaml.

records.heading: config: site.session.key
comment: Cookie name

records.heading: config: site.session.same_site
comment: SameSite cookie attribute (strict|lax|none)
Required for Stripe/OAuth redirects - 'strict' blocks cookies on cross-site GET navigations

records.heading: config: site.session.httponly
comment: Prevent JavaScript access to cookies (always true in Rack)

records.heading: config: site.middleware.static_files
comment: Serve static files for frontend vue application

records.heading: config: site.middleware.utf8_sanitizer
comment: Sanitizes request parameters to ensure proper UTF-8 encoding
Prevents encoding-based attacks and malformed input

records.heading: config: site.middleware.authenticity_token
comment: Protects against Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) attacks
Validates that requests originate from the same site

records.heading: config: site.middleware.http_origin
comment: Protects against Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) attacks
Validates HTTP Origin header matches expected origin

records.heading: config: site.middleware.xss_header
comment: Sets X-XSS-Protection header to enable browser XSS filtering
Modern browsers rely less on this as CSP becomes standard

records.heading: config: site.middleware.frame_options
comment: Prevents your site from being embedded in frames (clickjacking protection)
Sets X-Frame-Options header to SAMEORIGIN or DENY

records.heading: config: site.middleware.path_traversal
comment: Blocks directory traversal attacks using "../" in paths
Critical for preventing unauthorized file access

records.heading: config: site.middleware.cookie_tossing
comment: Refuses (403) a request whose Cookie header carries the session cookie
(site.session.key) more than once, so a cookie planted by a sibling or
parent host cannot compete with the real one (Onetime::Middleware::
CookieTossing, RISK-2026-08-14-COOKIE-TOSSING). Default on since
v0.26.14; set MIDDLEWARE_COOKIE_TOSSING=false to disable.

records.heading: config: site.middleware.ip_spoofing
comment: Prevents IP spoofing attacks by validating IP addresses
Useful when IP-based access controls are implemented

records.heading: config: site.middleware.strict_transport
comment: Forces all connections to use HTTPS via HSTS headers
Disable only for development or when behind a secure proxy

records.heading: config: site.middleware.profiles.authenticated_web.deflater
comment: Gzip response compression via Rack::Deflater

records.heading: config: site.middleware.profiles.authenticated_web.content_security_policy
comment: Content-Security-Policy header via Rack::Protection

records.heading: config: site.middleware.profiles.authenticated_web.frame_options
comment: X-Frame-Options clickjacking protection

records.heading: config: site.middleware.profiles.authenticated_web.http_origin
comment: Origin-based CSRF protection with a display-domain allow_if

records.heading: config: site.middleware.profiles.authenticated_web.ip_spoofing
comment: Rejects requests with disagreeing forwarded-IP headers

records.heading: config: site.middleware.profiles.authenticated_web.path_traversal
comment: Normalizes "../" segments out of request paths

records.heading: config: site.middleware.profiles.authenticated_web.session_hijacking
comment: Ties the session to stable client attributes

records.heading: config: site.network.trusted_proxy.enabled
comment: Turns proxy-aware IP resolution on. The mode, header, cidrs, and
depth settings below do nothing while this is false.
When false, forwarded headers are ignored and the client IP is
REMOTE_ADDR — the address that opened the connection. That is right
only when clients connect to the app directly: put a
proxy in front and REMOTE_ADDR is the proxy, so every request looks
like it came from one address. When true, the client IP is read out
of the forwarded headers using `mode` below. Behind a proxy you
control, you want true. Behind one you cannot configure to overwrite
X-Forwarded-For, set true and set `mode` to depth, which picks the
client by its position in the chain so a forged entry is never
reached.

records.heading: config: site.network.trusted_proxy.mode
comment: How to resolve client IP behind proxies:
'filter' (default): CIDR-walk. Otto::Utils.resolve_client_ip walks the
forwarded chain LEFT-TO-RIGHT and returns the first entry that is not
in the trusted-proxy set — i.e. the LEFTMOST non-proxy entry becomes
the client IP. The trusted set is the RFC1918/loopback/link-local
private ranges (always trusted in this mode) plus every range in
`cidrs` below. Works for most k8s/cloud deployments where the proxy
tier has enumerable internal addresses. Note: filter mode reads the
X-Forwarded-For family only (X-Forwarded-For, X-Real-IP, X-Client-IP)
and REJECTS any other `header` value below at boot.
SECURITY — read before enabling: the edge proxy MUST OVERWRITE
X-Forwarded-For with the real peer address so the resolved client IP
is always proxy-attested:
nginx:  proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $remote_addr;
Caddy:  header_up X-Forwarded-For {remote_host}
Use 'depth' instead when you cannot make the edge overwrite: it counts
positions from the right, so a forged leftmost entry is never reached.
'depth': Position-based counting. Skip exactly N rightmost hops.
Use when:
- CDN has a public IP (not RFC1918)
- Variable proxy depth that filter can't handle
- You need deterministic hop selection regardless of IP class
- Your edge appends to X-Forwarded-For and you cannot change it
When filter and depth differ:
- CDN with public IP: filter returns CDN IP (add to cidrs or use depth)
- Variable hop count: filter handles automatically; depth fails if wrong
- Forged leftmost entry: filter returns it (see SECURITY above); depth
ignores it, since only the position N-from-the-right is read
Matched case-insensitively and canonicalized (like `header` below). The
set is closed: any other value falls back to filter — the safer mode —
and WARNs at boot naming the value, rather than failing the boot. The
'filter' default here is documentation; the app applies the same default
itself, so an unset or programmatically assembled config behaves
identically.

records.heading: config: site.network.trusted_proxy.header
comment: Depth mode only: which header to read the forwarding chain from.
The accepted set is closed — exactly one of:
- X-Forwarded-For: Most common (nginx, Caddy, HAProxy, AWS ALB/ELB,
Cloudflare, Fastly, most k8s ingresses)
- Forwarded: RFC 7239 standard; IPv6 addresses are bracketed,
e.g. for="[2001:db8::1]". HAProxy and Apache can emit it, but it
remains uncommon in practice
- Both: Try Forwarded first, fall back to X-Forwarded-For
Matched case-insensitively and canonicalized; any other value raises
at boot instead of silently resolving from the wrong header.
Vendor client-IP headers are NOT selectable — CF-Connecting-IP,
True-Client-IP and friends are never read for client-IP resolution,
and they carry a single address rather than a chain, so there are no
hops to count. (Vendor GEO headers such as CF-IPCountry are a separate
concern with its own resolution path; this setting does not affect
them.) If the edge only sets one of those, have it write the chain
into X-Forwarded-For. Filter mode reads the X-Forwarded-For family
only (X-Forwarded-For, X-Real-IP, X-Client-IP) and never RFC 7239
Forwarded: with `mode: filter`, any value here other than
X-Forwarded-For FAILS THE BOOT with a message naming both keys.
Leave it at the default (or unset) unless mode is depth.

records.heading: config: site.network.trusted_proxy.cidrs
comment: Filter mode only: Additional CIDR ranges to trust as proxies
beyond RFC1918 defaults. Use when your CDN or proxy has public IPs.

records.heading: config: site.network.trusted_proxy.depth
comment: Depth mode only: Number of proxy hops to skip from the right.
1 = standard single reverse proxy (nginx/Caddy)
2 = CDN → reverse proxy → app
No-proxy / direct connection: set enabled: false above rather
than depth: 0; the master switch falls back to REMOTE_ADDR.

records.heading: config: site.network.geo.header
comment: Optional app-level geo header, checked BEFORE the built-in vendor
headers. FILTER MODE ONLY — setting it under depth mode would trip
Otto's boot-time depth/geo_header conflict, so it is ignored there.
Leave blank to use only the built-in vendor headers (e.g. CF-IPCountry).

records.heading: config: site.network.geo.db_path
comment: Optional path to a local MaxMind-format country database (.mmdb) for
deployments without a geo-tagging CDN (direct-connect, or depth mode).
Looked up on the ALREADY-MASKED IP, so raw addresses never reach it.
Works in ALL modes. Requires the optional 'maxmind-db' gem; a bad path
or missing gem fails at boot (not per-request). Blank = disabled.

records.heading: config: site.network.assume_https
comment: Assume HTTPS at the origin (opt-in, INDEPENDENT of trusted_proxy).
Upgrade-only: when true, requests that do not already look like HTTPS
are marked as HTTPS before any downstream consumer reads the scheme
(Secure session cookie, HttpOrigin, CSRF, HSTS, scheme redirects).
Only enable when a real TLS-terminating proxy fronts the origin AND it
does NOT forward X-Forwarded-Proto: https (e.g. Cloudflare Tunnel).
Standard nginx/Caddy/ALB setups forward the scheme and do NOT need
this. Never enable on a directly-reachable origin: it would let a
plain-HTTP client be treated as HTTPS. Also keep site.ssl at its https
default when this is on: pairing assume_https with site.ssl:false makes
config-driven share/email/redirect links emit http:// while clients use
https (mixed-content downgrade of generated URLs).

records.heading: config: site.network.public_host_rewrite
comment: Public host rewrite (opt-in, default off).
For installs behind a proxy that rewrites Host to the origin target
and sends the public hostname in X-Forwarded-Host. When true, a request
classified as a canonical host, a subdomain of one, or a registered
custom domain has its Host set to that hostname before the mounted
apps run, so code that reads the request host directly sees the same
host as the rest of the application. The Host header as received stays
available in env['onetime.original_http_host']. Requests that do not
classify, and requests whose Host already names the public host, are
left as they are. No effect behind a proxy that preserves Host and
overwrites or removes X-Forwarded-Host.
The public port comes from the trusted proxy, never from an origin-hop
Host: the port in X-Forwarded-Host or, when that is a bare hostname,
a single-valued X-Forwarded-Port. The scheme-default port is left out.
See docs/operations/proxy-authority-header.md.
Since unreleased

records.heading: config: site.admin.allowed_hosts
comment: Which HOSTNAMES serve the Colonel admin surfaces (/colonel shell and
/api/colonel API). A request whose validated detected host is not on this
list receives the same 404 as the CIDR gate below.
Unset (default): ENFORCED, anchored on the canonical hosts —
features.domains.default and site.host, each with its www. variant. A
stock canonical deployment sees no change; tenant custom domains and
operator link-pool domains (features.domains.link_domains) stop serving
the admin console, which is the point.
Set but BLANK (ADMIN_ALLOWED_HOSTS="" or only whitespace/commas): the
same anchor fallback as unset at runtime, plus a boot WARN (#4127) — the
operator wrote an allowlist that names nothing, and on a localhost or
bare-IP install that written config yields no host gate at all (the
anchors have nothing to anchor on, so the gate self-disables below).
Set to serve admin on its own hostname (recommended; pair it with an edge
rule that 404s /colonel and /api/colonel on every OTHER vhost). Explicit
entries are matched LITERALLY — list the www. form too if you need it.
ADMIN_ALLOWED_HOSTS=admin.example.com
"*" ANYWHERE in the list disables the host gate entirely and logs a WARN
at boot; any other entry beside it is ignored (and named in a second
WARN). The CIDR gate is unaffected. This is the escape hatch for installs
reached by bare IP or by a hostname that is not the canonical domain.
Matching is case-insensitive, port-stripped and trailing-dot-stripped.
ASCII/A-label only: there is no IDN library in this project, so an
internationalized domain must be given in its punycode (xn--) form.
UNUSABLE ENTRIES — a wildcard pattern (*.example.com), a non-ASCII name,
a localhost form, or an IP literal — can never match a detected host.
Each is dropped and named in a boot WARN. If NOTHING in an explicitly set
list survives, the gate stays ACTIVE with an EMPTY allowlist: /colonel and
/api/colonel 404 on every hostname, rather than the admin console being
served on every hostname. The operator asked to restrict it, and a typo
must not produce the opposite. Onetime::Config.check_admin_allowed_hosts
says so at boot (WARN); it does NOT abort the boot, because the surfaces
are already fail-closed and the rest of the app is innocent.
Set "*" to turn the gate off on purpose.
The forwarded host header (X-Forwarded-Host) only counts toward this
gate when
site.network.trusted_proxy is configured AND the peer passed it. Behind a
proxy that forwards the public hostname instead of rewriting Host, set
trusted_proxy or both admin surfaces 404 (see
docs/operations/admin-network-isolation.md).
INACTIVE only when this list is UNSET and neither canonical anchor is a
hostname the app could ever detect — the stock local-dev and bare-IP
self-hosted posture (site.host defaults to localhost:3000). The gate
self-disables and logs a WARN at boot rather than locking the admin
surfaces out of installs that have no routable hostname to anchor on.
This exemption never applies to a list an operator set (above).
Boot logs the effective posture of both factors on one INFO line, "Admin
surface isolation posture", including the site.network.trusted_proxy
state — with no trusted proxy declared, both gates judge inputs any peer
on a private address can influence.
NO `|| []` FALLBACK HERE — deliberate (#4127). Unset must render nil and
a set-but-blank value (ADMIN_ALLOWED_HOSTS="" or whitespace/commas only)
must render a list with nothing in it, because
Onetime::Config.check_admin_allowed_hosts WARNs at boot on the second
shape and stays silent on the first. Folding both to [] here made an
explicitly written blank allowlist indistinguishable from no allowlist
at all. (DEFAULTS in lib/onetime/config.rb carries no allowed_hosts key
for the same reason — deep_merge would resolve nil back to it.)

records.heading: config: site.admin.allowed_cidrs
comment: Optional network isolation for the Colonel admin surfaces (/colonel shell
and /api/colonel API). When set to a non-empty list of CIDR ranges, any
request whose trusted-proxy-resolved client IP falls OUTSIDE the allowlist
receives a 404 (indistinguishable-from-absent, not a 403) on both
surfaces. This is defense-in-depth ON TOP OF the two app-layer auth layers
(role=colonel at the router + verify_one_of_roles!(colonel:true) in each
logic class), which still enforce beneath it.
Empty/unset (default): NO-OP. Both surfaces stay reachable and the auth
layers are the sole gate — the correct posture for self-hosted
single-container installs, which cannot require a VPN. A list that IS set
but where no entry parses as a CIDR is the opposite case and denies both
surfaces (with an ERROR at boot): a list an operator wrote is never
silently disabled. Set this on cloud
deployments to private ranges only (e.g. a Tailscale/VPN CGNAT range like
100.64.0.0/10, or an office RFC1918 range). Self-hosted operators who want
isolation without app config can instead front the surfaces with a reverse
proxy (see docs/operations/admin-network-isolation.md).
IMPORTANT: resolution uses the trusted-proxy-aware client IP, so behind a
reverse proxy you must also configure site.network.trusted_proxy or every
request resolves to the proxy hop. A raw X-Forwarded-For header cannot
bypass the allowlist.
Entries may be as fine as a single host (/32, IPv6 /128): membership is
judged against the full-precision resolved client IP, even though request
logs carry only its privacy-masked form. An entry that does not parse as
a CIDR is dropped and named in a boot WARN.

records.heading: config: site.admin.rodauth_admin_url
comment: Base URL of the standalone Rodauth Admin instance (onetimesecret/
rodauth-admin), the tool that administers the SQL-backed accounts in
full auth mode. Optional, no credential, and nothing is ever requested
from it: the colonel console only renders OUTBOUND links to it (the
customer page deep-links to the matching account by extid; the sessions
console links to it when it is not the session authority). Unset means
those links render as plain text. Mirrors COLONEL_CONSOLE_URL on the
admin side. Example: http://127.0.0.1:9292 (reached over an SSH tunnel).

records.heading: config: site.brand_pack
comment: Brand pack selection (#3739, v2 #3774). A brand pack is the single unit of
branding: a directory of root-served assets (favicon.ico, icon-*.png,
site.webmanifest, etc.) plus an optional brand.yaml identity manifest
(colours, product name — absorbed into the brand: block below at boot, as a
fallback beneath operator config and BRAND_* env).
Resolution ALWAYS lands on a pack: an unset brand_pack resolves to the
tracked `default` pack (public/branding/default, the neutral keyhole set).
A brand_pack NAME is resolved across two search roots, first existing wins:
1. etc/branding/<name>     — operator space (runtime mounts / confext)
2. public/branding/<name>  — vendor space (tracked default + generated packs)
brand_assets_dir (an explicit path, e.g. a runtime mount) wins over
brand_pack; a missing path or unknown name falls back to the default pack.

records.heading: config: internationalization.date_format
comment: Date/time display format. Accepts a preset keyword or a date-fns pattern.
Setting date_format alone controls both date-only and date+time display.
Set datetime_format only if you need a different format for date+time contexts.
Presets:
locale  - browser-native formatting (default)
long    - March 21, 2026 / March 21, 2026 2:30 PM
Or pass a raw date-fns pattern: https://date-fns.org/docs/format

records.heading: config: diagnostics.enabled
comment: If this is false, the rest of the settings are ignored

records.heading: config: site.secret_options.default_ttl
comment: Default Time-To-Live (TTL) for secrets in seconds
This value is used if no specific TTL is provided when creating a secret

records.heading: config: site.secret_options.ttl_options
comment: Available TTL options for secret creation (in seconds)
These options will be presented to users when they create a new secret
Format: String of integers representing seconds

records.heading: config: site.secret_options.ttl_max_anonymous
comment: Maximum TTL for secrets created without an account (anonymous callers).
Default: 604800 (7 days) — a sane default, not a hard limit. Self-hosted
deployments may raise or lower it; the effective ceiling is the lower of
this value and the ttl_options maximum, bounded by 365 days. When billing
is enabled the free-tier plan limit applies as well, so the anonymous
grant never exceeds what an authenticated free-tier user receives.
PLAN_TTL_ANONYMOUS is the deprecated alias, read only here — this line is
the single place the old name survives. The ceiling itself is read from
the resolved config key (site.secret_options.ttl_max_anonymous) via
WithEntitlements.configured_anonymous_max_ttl, never from the env var.
Organization.free_tier_limits does read ENV['TTL_MAX_ANONYMOUS'] directly
for its secret_lifetime fallback, and does not honour the alias.

records.heading: config: site.secret_options.passphrase.required
comment: Require users to enter a passphrase when creating secrets

records.heading: config: site.secret_options.passphrase.minimum_length
comment: Minimum number of characters required for passphrases
Default to 4 chars to prevent trivially guessable passphrases while
maintaining backward compatibility with existing integrations.

records.heading: config: site.secret_options.passphrase.maximum_length
comment: Maximum number of characters allowed for passphrases

records.heading: config: site.secret_options.passphrase.enforce_complexity
comment: Enforce complexity requirements (uppercase, lowercase, numbers, symbols)

records.heading: config: site.secret_options.content.maximum_length
comment: Maximum number of characters allowed in a secret's body. Enforced
server-side on secret creation and used as the single source of
truth for the client-side textarea limit.

records.heading: config: site.secret_options.generated_value_display_ttl
comment: How long (in seconds) a generated password remains visible on the
receipt page after creation. Set to 0 to disable receipt-page display.

records.heading: config: site.secret_options.create_rate_limit.max_per_ip
comment: Anonymous creations permitted per window from a single masked client IP.
The bucket is a whole /24 (office, campus NAT), and behind an
unconfigured reverse proxy it is the entire deployment — so this is
deliberately loose (10x the signup/reset caps) because secret creation is
the core product action. Raise it for dense-NAT populations; a too-tight
value here is an outage of secret creation for a whole neighborhood.

records.heading: config: site.secret_options.create_rate_limit.window
comment: Counting window in seconds (1 hour).

records.heading: config: site.secret_options.create_rate_limit.lockout
comment: Lockout duration in seconds once the cap is hit (1 hour).

records.heading: config: site.secret_options.password_generation.default_length
comment: Default length for generated passwords

records.heading: config: site.secret_options.password_generation.maximum_length
comment: Server-enforced ceiling on requested generated-password length.
Rejects oversized `length` values before allocation (DoS guard);
matches the frontend Zod max so the two limits stay in lockstep.

records.heading: config: site.secret_options.password_generation.character_sets.uppercase
comment: Include uppercase letters (A-Z)

records.heading: config: site.secret_options.password_generation.character_sets.lowercase
comment: Include lowercase letters (a-z)

records.heading: config: site.secret_options.password_generation.character_sets.numbers
comment: Include numbers (0-9)

records.heading: config: site.secret_options.password_generation.character_sets.exclude_ambiguous
comment: Exclude ambiguous characters (0, O, l, 1, I) to prevent confusion

records.heading: config: site.authentication.enabled
comment: Can be disabled altogether, including API authentication.

records.heading: config: site.authentication.signup
comment: Allow users to create accounts. This can be disabled if you plan
to create accounts manually or enable during setup when accounts
can be created and then disabled to prevent any new users from
creating accounts.

records.heading: config: site.authentication.signin
comment: Generally if you allow registration, you allow signin. But there
are circumstances where it's helpful to turn off authentication
temporarily.

records.heading: config: site.authentication.autoverify
comment: By default, new accounts need to verify their email address before
they can sign in. This is a security measure to prevent spamming
and abuse of the system. If you're running a private instance or
an instance for your team or company, you can disable this feature
to make it easier for users to sign in.

records.heading: config: site.authentication.required
comment: When enabled, the homepage secret form is not available unless
the user is logged in. Similar to a disabled homepage, but still
shows the header with logo and navigation links. This allows for
a more restrictive mode where only authenticated users can create
secrets while maintaining site navigation and branding.

records.heading: config: site.authentication.allowed_signup_domains
comment: Colonel (admin) accounts are managed via the CLI:
bin/ots customers role promote user@example.com
bin/ots customers role demote user@example.com
bin/ots customers role list
Restrict account creation to specific email domains while allowing
secret-sharing with any email address. When set, only email addresses
from the listed domains can create accounts. This is useful for
organizations that want to limit signups to their own domains while
still allowing secrets to be shared with anyone.
Format: List of domain names (e.g., example.com, company.org)
If empty or not set, signups are allowed from any domain (default).
Environment variable: ALLOWED_SIGNUP_DOMAIN (comma-separated list)

records.heading: config: site.authentication.reset_request_rate_limit.max_per_ip
comment: Requests permitted per window from a single client IP.

records.heading: config: site.authentication.reset_request_rate_limit.max_per_email
comment: Higher backstop cap per submitted login (catches IP rotation).

records.heading: config: site.authentication.reset_request_rate_limit.window
comment: Counting window in seconds (1 hour).

records.heading: config: site.authentication.reset_request_rate_limit.lockout
comment: Lockout duration in seconds once a tier's cap is hit (1 hour).

records.heading: config: site.authentication.email_login_request_rate_limit.enabled
comment: Since unreleased

records.heading: config: site.authentication.email_login_request_rate_limit.max_per_ip
comment: Requests permitted per window from a single masked client IP. Looser
than the reset-request cap: a magic link is a sign-in method, and a
whole /24 (an office NAT) shares this bucket.
Since unreleased

records.heading: config: site.authentication.email_login_request_rate_limit.max_per_email
comment: Backstop cap per submitted login (catches IP rotation). Keep
max_per_email >= 2 * max_per_ip AND lockout >= window: a single IP
timing its requests around its own window boundary lands up to
2 * max_per_ip - 2 requests in one login's window, and with a shorter
lockout it is free again inside that window, so one source could lock
a victim out of magic-link sign-in from every IP. The defaults
(30/90, 3600/3600) satisfy both. Rodauth's resend window already caps
the mail an account receives.
Since unreleased

records.heading: config: site.authentication.email_login_request_rate_limit.window
comment: Counting window in seconds (1 hour).
Since unreleased

records.heading: config: site.authentication.email_login_request_rate_limit.lockout
comment: Lockout duration in seconds once a tier's cap is hit (1 hour). Keep it
>= window (see max_per_email).
Since unreleased

records.heading: config: site.authentication.create_account_rate_limit.max_per_ip
comment: Signups permitted per window from a single masked client IP. The bucket
is a whole /24 (office, campus NAT), and behind an unconfigured reverse
proxy it is the entire deployment — so this is deliberately loose
relative to the one signup a person needs. Raise it for dense-NAT
populations; a too-tight value here is a signup-funnel outage.

records.heading: config: site.authentication.create_account_rate_limit.window
comment: Counting window in seconds (1 hour).

records.heading: config: site.authentication.create_account_rate_limit.lockout
comment: Lockout duration in seconds once the cap is hit (1 hour).

records.heading: config: brand.logo_dark_url

records.heading: config: brand.apple_touch_icon_url

records.heading: config: features.regions.jurisdictions

Environment Variable Format:
JURISDICTIONS=ID:domain,ID:domain,...
where ID is the jurisdiction identifier (e.g., EU, CA, US)
and domain is the hostname for that jurisdiction
Examples:
JURISDICTIONS=EU:eu.example.com,CA:ca.example.com
JURISDICTIONS=US:us.onetimesecret.com,EU:eu.onetimesecret.com,APAC:apac.onetimesecret.com

records.heading: config: features.incoming.enabled
comment: Enable or disable the incoming secrets feature.
This flag governs the CANONICAL domain only. Per-domain incoming on
custom domains is gated by the org's incoming_secrets entitlement plus a
ready IncomingConfig, NOT by this flag (see the canonical/custom split in
RecipientResolver / CustomDomain::HomepageConfig#incoming_available?). To
emergency-disable incoming on custom domains, revoke the incoming_secrets
entitlement or set ORGS_INCOMING_SECRETS_ENABLED=false.

records.heading: config: features.incoming.memo_max_length
comment: Maximum character length for the memo/subject field

records.heading: config: features.incoming.default_ttl
comment: Default TTL for incoming secrets in seconds (7 days = 604800)

records.heading: config: features.incoming.default_passphrase
comment: Optional default passphrase for all incoming secrets (nil = no passphrase)

records.heading: config: features.incoming.rate_limit.max_per_ip
comment: Submissions permitted per window from a single client IP.

records.heading: config: features.incoming.rate_limit.max_per_recipient
comment: Higher backstop cap per recipient hash (catches IP-rotating spam).

records.heading: config: features.incoming.rate_limit.window
comment: Counting window in seconds (1 hour).

records.heading: config: features.incoming.rate_limit.lockout
comment: Lockout duration in seconds once a tier's cap is hit (1 hour).

records.heading: config: features.domains.require_verified
comment: When true, secret creation rejects an unverified custom share_domain
with a form error, under every validation strategy. When false
(default), creation still requires the domain to be served (see
serve_unverified below). Canonical domains are unaffected.

records.heading: config: features.domains.serve_unverified
comment: Under a validation_strategy that checks ownership (approximated,
caddy_on_demand), a registered custom domain is served only once its
ownership is verified, by its TXT record or an operator override.
Until then its host answers 404 for every path, and the domain is not
offered for links. Under passthrough, registration by the owning
organization is enough. A domain record with no organization is never
served.
When true, every registered custom domain that has an organization
is served whatever its ownership state, and a warning is logged at
boot. Only the value true enables it.
Since unreleased

records.heading: config: features.domains.default
comment: The default domain used for link URLs. When not set or empty,
site.host is used.

records.heading: config: features.domains.link_domains
comment: LINK_DOMAINS — comma-separated hosts offered in the link-domain
picker. For installs whose canonical host is an internal platform
address (e.g. ge-abcd123.eu.otshosted.com) that must keep serving
the app but must never be offered to customers as a link domain.
Three-way semantics — all deliberate:
unset          -> the picker offers the canonical domain
(every pre-existing install is unchanged)
set            -> the picker offers exactly these hosts; the
canonical domain appears only if listed
set-but-empty  -> boot error naming LINK_DOMAINS
(Onetime::Config.validate_link_domains!)
A set list that names only UNPARSEABLE hosts is the same boot
error: there is no safe fallback for it. Offering the canonical
domain instead would contradict the request (hiding that host is
the whole point), and offering nothing leaves the picker empty, so
the typo has to fail loud. A list that mixes good and bad entries
boots — the bad one is dropped and logged.
This is NOT a UI-only setting: every entry joins the canonical
host set, so requests to these hosts are classified :canonical and
serve the app instead of being rejected as :invalid.
The `&.` chain is load-bearing — it is what keeps unset (nil) and
set-but-empty ([]) distinguishable through ERB+YAML. Do NOT copy
the `|| nil` idiom used by `default:` above; it collapses the two.
`link_domains` is also deliberately absent from Config::DEFAULTS —
deep_merge restores the default for any nil in loaded config,
which would make set-but-empty undetectable.

records.heading: config: features.domains.validation_strategy
comment: Domain validation and certificate management strategy
Options:
- passthrough: No validation or cert management
- approximated: Use approximated.app API for SSL certs and validation (requires cluster config)
- caddy_on_demand: Use Caddy's on-demand TLS (requires internal ACME endpoint).
Ownership is checked with our own DNS lookup of the domain's TXT
challenge record; Caddy issuing a certificate does not verify a domain.
Resolving and SSL status come from our own A/AAAA lookup and a TLS
handshake to the domain on port 443, so the application host needs
outbound DNS and outbound TCP 443.

records.heading: config: features.domains.acme.listen_address
comment: IP address to bind to in standalone mode (should always be localhost)

records.heading: config: features.domains.acme.port
comment: Port for standalone mode (Caddy's ask directive points here)

records.heading: config: features.organizations.homepage_network_rules_ui_enabled

Default OFF. Turning it off stops edits only: rules already stored

Since unreleased

records.heading: config: features.organizations.base_domain_signup_enabled
comment: Lets organizations with the base_domain_signup entitlement admit their
custom domain's own base domain to its sign-up allowlist automatically
(secrets.acme.com admits @acme.com). Also checked when a sign-up is
validated, so turning it off stops a saved setting from admitting
anyone.
Since unreleased

records.heading: config: features.organizations.audit_logs_enabled
comment: Gates exposure (UI + list API) of the organization secret-activity
trail; pairs with the `audit_logs` entitlement. Defaults ON, unlike
the sibling flags above, because the trail ships working out of the
box — this is an opt-out exclusion (ORGS_AUDIT_LOGS_ENABLED=false),
not an opt-in feature. Does not stop event collection.

records.heading: config: features.secret_activity.collect
comment: When false, event recording pauses; existing events stay readable.

records.heading: config: features.secret_activity.max_events
comment: Newest events retained per organization (floor: 100). Lowering this
deletes (not hides) each org's oldest events on its next write.

records.heading: config: features.secret_activity.geo_country_enabled
comment: Country-level geo capture on Secret Activity events (#3989). A distinct
axis from `collect`: gates ONLY the net_country attribute, pending
counsel review of org-tier geo exposure (ADR-021 Decision 4 open
question; ADR-022 does not yet cover this attribute). Defaults OFF
(opt-in) — the inverse polarity of the sibling flags — because this is
the not-yet-reviewed surface, not an already-approved one.

records.heading: config: features.markdown.enabled
comment: Since unreleased

records.heading: config: redis.uri
comment: Redis/Valkey connection URI - Compatible with Redis, Valkey, and other
Redis-compatible servers.
Environment Variable Precedence (highest to lowest):
1. VALKEY_URL or REDIS_URL - Explicit connection string
2. IN_DOCKER=1 - Force Docker configuration (redis://host.docker.internal:6379)
3. AUTO_DETECT_DOCKER=1 - Enable automatic Docker detection via /.dockerenv file
4. Default - Local development (redis://CHANGEME@127.0.0.1:6379)
Format: redis://[:password@]host[:port]/[db-number]
Examples:
- redis://mypassword@localhost:6379       # Simple password auth
- redis://user:pass@localhost:6379        # Username/password auth
- redis://host.docker.internal:6379       # Docker environment
- redis://127.0.0.1:6379                  # Local development

records.heading: config: redis.require_tls
comment: Require TLS to the datastore (RISK-2026-08-14-L07). When true, boot
refuses to start unless the URI above uses rediss:// or valkeys:// (with
no `ssl` query parameter, which would override the scheme), whatever the
host. When false (the default, so existing deployments keep booting), a
plaintext URI is reported once at boot, graded by where the host is:
- a dotted hostname or public IP: a WARNING — the datastore password,
session data and secrets would cross the network unencrypted;
- a single-label name (a compose service such as `maindb`) or a private,
fe80::/10): an INFO line, so the default compose stack does not warn
on every boot;
- loopback or a unix socket: nothing.
The host graded is the one the client connects to, including a `host` or
`path` query parameter. Hostnames are never resolved. Set
VALKEY_REQUIRE_TLS=true or REDIS_REQUIRE_TLS=true (either one enables it).
See lib/onetime/initializers/configure_familia.rb.
Since unreleased

records.heading: config: jobs.enabled
comment: Global toggle for background job system

records.heading: config: jobs.rabbitmq_url
comment: RabbitMQ connection URL
Format: amqp://[user:password@]host[:port][/vhost]
The vhost dev doesn't exist in RabbitMQ. Either create it:
rabbitmqctl add_vhost dev
rabbitmqctl set_permissions -p dev guest ".*" ".*" ".*"

records.heading: config: jobs.channel_pool_size
comment: Publisher settings (Puma process)
Channel pool size for multi-threaded web server

records.heading: config: jobs.fallback_to_sync
comment: Fallback to synchronous delivery when RabbitMQ unavailable
Recommended: true for production to ensure emails always send

records.heading: config: jobs.domain_refresh.check_interval
comment: How often to refresh (rufus-scheduler interval)

records.heading: config: jobs.domain_refresh.batch_size
comment: Maximum domains processed per run (rate limiting)

records.heading: config: jobs.domain_refresh.dns_propagation_window
comment: Seconds to pause between domains within a run. Leave unset to use the
validation strategy's own pacing (approximated: 0.5 for its API rate
cap; caddy_on_demand and passthrough: none). Any number, including 0,
overrides the strategy.
rate_limit: 0.5  # Since v0.25.2
DNS-propagation warm-up: domains created within this window that are
still not fully verified (verified=false OR resolving=false) fill any
capacity left after the paged walk, without exceeding batch_size.
Set to '0' to disable.

records.heading: config: jobs.expiration_warnings.enabled
comment: Enable/disable expiration warning emails

records.heading: config: jobs.expiration_warnings.check_interval
comment: How often to scan for expiring secrets (rufus-scheduler interval)

records.heading: config: jobs.expiration_warnings.warning_hours
comment: Warn once a secret is within N hours of expiring. The warning is sent on
the next scan, so it arrives between N and (N - check_interval) hours
before expiry.

records.heading: config: jobs.expiration_warnings.min_ttl_hours
comment: Only warn for secrets with TTL greater than this (hours)
Prevents spamming for short-lived secrets

records.heading: config: jobs.expiration_warnings.batch_size
comment: Maximum warnings to process per job run (rate limiting)
Prevents queue overflow; remaining secrets processed in next run

records.heading: config: jobs.favicon_fetch.enabled
comment: Feature flag — default ON (see #3780)

records.heading: config: jobs.favicon_fetch.timeout
comment: Seconds per HTTP fetch (connect + read)

records.heading: config: jobs.favicon_fetch.max_response_bytes
comment: Response size ceiling in bytes (100 KB), streamed-enforced

records.heading: config: jobs.favicon_fetch.max_redirects
comment: Maximum redirects followed, each re-validated against the SSRF guard

records.heading: config: jobs.favicon_backfill.enabled
comment: Feature flag — default OFF

records.heading: config: jobs.favicon_backfill.cron
comment: Scan schedule (cron); nightly at 03:00 by default

records.heading: config: jobs.favicon_backfill.batch_size
comment: Domains loaded+scanned per page while paginating the full set

records.heading: config: jobs.favicon_backfill.max_attempts
comment: Stop retrying a domain after this many terminal non-success attempts

records.heading: config: jobs.favicon_backfill.base_days
comment: Backoff base in days (doubles each attempt: 1, 2, 4, 8, ...)

records.heading: config: jobs.favicon_backfill.cap_days
comment: Backoff ceiling in days (the doubling never schedules further out than this)

records.heading: config: jobs.maintenance.enabled

records.heading: config: emailer.mode
comment: Production Settings (for reference)

records.heading: config: emailer.sender_provider
comment: Provider for custom mail sender domain provisioning (DNS/DKIM).
When set, decouples domain provisioning from the sending transport.
Valid values: ses, sendgrid, lettermint, smtp2go, smtp
If unset, falls back to mode (EMAILER_MODE).

records.heading: config: emailer.pass
comment: The double quotes are important b/c credentials can have characters that break YAML parsing.

records.heading: config: emailer.ssl
comment: Since unreleased

records.heading: config: emailer.feedback_to
comment: Recipient ("To:") address for /feedback submissions.
When set, feedback emails are delivered here instead of the first colonel
in the database. Useful for routing to a shared inbox or alias.

records.heading: config: emailer.show_logo
comment: Whether to include the logo image in HTML emails (default: false).
Set to true only when recipients can reach the app's base URI to
load the image; otherwise a broken image looks less trustworthy.

records.heading: config: email_providers.ses.region
comment: AWS region for SES sender-domain provisioning (the SESv2 API client used
to create/get/delete email identities). This is independent of
EMAILER_REGION, which configures the install-level transactional mailer.
For data-residency, use a regional endpoint such as ca-central-1 (Canada)
or ap-southeast-2 (Sydney). Confirm SES is available in the region.
Override via CUSTOM_MAIL_SES_REGION env var

records.heading: config: email_providers.ses.access_key_id
comment: AWS credentials for the SES provisioning API client, kept independent of
the SMTP/transactional mailer credentials. build_provider_config('ses')
otherwise resolves the key pair from emailer.user/pass (i.e.
SMTP_USERNAME/SMTP_PASSWORD when EMAILER_MODE=smtp), which would silently
use the SMTP login as the AWS key. These dedicated knobs fall back to the
standard AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID / AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY and, when set, override
the emailer-derived values. Leave unset only when SES is also the delivery
backend (EMAILER_MODE=ses) and the emailer already carries the AWS keys.
Override via CUSTOM_MAIL_SES_ACCESS_KEY_ID / CUSTOM_MAIL_SES_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY

records.heading: config: email_providers.ses.dkim_selector_count
comment: Number of DKIM selectors (SES uses 3 by default)

records.heading: config: email_providers.ses.spf_include
comment: SPF include domain

records.heading: config: email_providers.sendgrid.subdomain
comment: Branding subdomain prefix (appears in CNAME records)
Override via CUSTOM_MAIL_SENDGRID_SUBDOMAIN env var

records.heading: config: email_providers.sendgrid.spf_include
comment: SPF include domain

records.heading: config: email_providers.lettermint.api_token
comment: Project token for Lettermint Sending API (email delivery)
Required when emailer.mode is 'lettermint'
Override via LETTERMINT_API_TOKEN env var

records.heading: config: email_providers.lettermint.team_token
comment: Team token for Lettermint Team API (domain provisioning)
Required for custom mail sender domain management
Override via LETTERMINT_TEAM_TOKEN env var

records.heading: config: email_providers.lettermint.api_base_url
comment: API base URL (for enterprise/on-premise deployments)
Override via LETTERMINT_BASE_URL env var

records.heading: config: email_providers.lettermint.spf_cname_prefix
comment: SPF CNAME subdomain prefix (e.g., 'lm-bounces' creates lm-bounces.yourdomain.com)
Override via CUSTOM_MAIL_LETTERMINT_SPF_CNAME_PREFIX env var

records.heading: config: email_providers.lettermint.spf_cname_target
comment: SPF CNAME target domain (Lettermint maintains SPF at this target)
Override via CUSTOM_MAIL_LETTERMINT_SPF_CNAME_TARGET env var

records.heading: config: email_providers.smtp2go.api_key
comment: API key for the SMTP2GO API (email delivery and domain provisioning)
Required when emailer.mode is 'smtp2go'
Override via SMTP2GO_API_KEY env var

records.heading: config: email_providers.smtp2go.api_base_url
comment: API base URL
Override via SMTP2GO_BASE_URL env var

records.heading: config: email_providers.smtp2go.returnpath_subdomain
comment: Return-path subdomain prefix (e.g., 'bounce' creates bounce.yourdomain.com)
Published by the customer as a CNAME record so the envelope sender
aligns with their domain for SPF. Provisioned via POST /domain/add.
Override via CUSTOM_MAIL_SMTP2GO_RETURNPATH_SUBDOMAIN env var

records.heading: config: email_providers.smtp2go.tracking_subdomain
comment: Tracking subdomain prefix (e.g., 'track' creates track.yourdomain.com)
Published by the customer as a CNAME record for open/click tracking.
Override via CUSTOM_MAIL_SMTP2GO_TRACKING_SUBDOMAIN env var

records.heading: config: email_providers.smtp2go.fastaccept
comment: Fast-accept mode. Default false = synchronous delivery accounting: the
response carries succeeded/failed/failures, so a failed recipient is
reported instead of silently dropped. Set true only to opt into
fire-and-forget (lower latency, no per-recipient failure detection).
Override via CUSTOM_MAIL_SMTP2GO_FASTACCEPT env var (true/false)

records.heading: config: mail.truemail.default_validation_type
comment: Available validation types: :regex, :mx, :mx_blacklist, :smtp

records.heading: config: mail.truemail.verifier_email
comment: Required for :smtp validation

records.heading: config: mail.truemail.allowed_domains_only
comment: :verifier_domain: <%= ENV['VERIFIER_DOMAIN'] || 'example.com' %>
:connection_timeout: 2
:response_timeout: 2
:connection_attempts: 3
:validation_type_for:
'example.com': :regex
Truemail will only validate email addresses that match the
domains listed in :allowed_domains. If the domain is not
listed, the email address will always be considered invalid.

records.heading: config: mail.truemail.smtp_fail_fast
comment: :smtp_port: 25
End smtp validation after the first invalid response rather than
retrying, followed by trying the next server. Can reduce the time
time to validate an email address, but may not catch all issues.

records.heading: config: mail.truemail.smtp_safe_check
comment: Parse the content of the SMTP error message to determine if the
email address is valid. This can be useful for some SMTP servers
that don't return exact answers.

records.heading: config: mail.truemail.not_rfc_mx_lookup_flow
comment: Whether to disable the RFC MX lookup flow. When true, only DNS
validation will be performed on MX and Null MX records.

records.heading: config: mail.truemail.logger.tracking_event
comment: One of: :error (default), :unrecognized_error, :recognized_error, :all.

records.heading: auth: mode
comment: Authentication mode: 'simple' (Redis-only) or 'full' (requires SQL db)
Can be overridden with AUTHENTICATION_MODE environment variable

records.heading: auth: simple
comment: Simple mode settings (Redis-only authentication)

records.heading: auth: full.database_url
comment: Application Connection
Used at runtime by the application.
e.g. "postgres://user:password@host:port/database"
SQLite paths:
sqlite::memory: - In-memory, no persistence (dev/test only)
sqlite://data/auth.db - Relative path from application directory
sqlite:///data/auth.db - Absolute path from filesystem root
sqlite:///tmp/auth.db - Temporary, lost on restart
⚠️  In OCI containers: SQLite files MUST be in a mounted volume directory
(e.g., /app/data or /data) or all data will be lost on container restart.
NOTE: The double quotes prevent YAML issues when parsing `sqlite::memory:`
NOTE: An exported-but-empty AUTH_DATABASE_URL is truthy in Ruby, so it is
normalized to unset here rather than rendering "" (which reaches
Sequel.connect as a schemeless URL). AuthConfig#database_url applies
the same rule for operator config files that do not.

records.heading: auth: full.database_url_migrations
comment: Migrations Connection (PostgreSQL, MySQL, MS SQL Server only)
Used at deployment time to run all Rodauth migrations:
- Set up the schema with appropriate permissions
- Create database functions for password verification
- Grant specific access to the application account as needed
When using this approach, the application account should only have EXECUTE
permission on the password hash verification functions and should not have
SELECT access to the password hash column.
Not needed for SQLite or other databases that don't support this security model.

records.heading: auth: full.restrict_to
records.rawValue: <%= [ENV['AUTH_PASSWORD_ONLY'] == 'true' && 'password', ENV['AUTH_EMAIL_AUTH_ONLY'] == 'true' && 'email_auth', ENV['AUTH_WEBAUTHN_ONLY'] == 'true' && 'webauthn', ENV['AUTH_SSO_ONLY'] == 'true' && 'sso'].select { |v| v }.then { |f| f.length == 1 && f.first || nil } %>

erb.raw: [ENV['AUTH_PASSWORD_ONLY'] == 'true' && 'password', ENV['AUTH_EMAIL_AUTH_ONLY'] == 'true' && 'email_auth', ENV['AUTH_WEBAUTHN_ONLY'] == 'true' && 'webauthn', ENV['AUTH_SSO_ONLY'] == 'true' && 'sso'].select { |v| v }.then { |f| f.length == 1 && f.first || nil }

comment: Restrict login page to a single authentication method
Values: password, email_auth, webauthn, sso
Leave blank to show all enabled authentication methods (default).
When set, only the specified method works on the sign-in surface — this
is an access control, not a display preference: every other method's
routes 404 (ADR-034#restrict-to-is-an-access-control-not-a-display-preference).
For sso: also disables password-based account management (destroy
account, change password, change email).
The underlying feature must also be enabled (e.g. restrict_to: sso
requires AUTH_SSO_ENABLED=true and at least one provider configured). If
it is not, boot fails — the restriction is never dropped to re-expose the
methods it was meant to hide. Unavailability that can only be seen after
boot, or on one host, degrades to "sign-in unavailable" instead
(ADR-034#degradation-is-fail-closed).
Set AT MOST ONE of AUTH_PASSWORD_ONLY / AUTH_EMAIL_AUTH_ONLY /
AUTH_WEBAUTHN_ONLY / AUTH_SSO_ONLY. Setting several renders nothing here
(there is no "restricted to two methods"), which on its own would be a
silent fail-open — so the ValidateAuthConfig initializer reads these four
env vars directly at boot and refuses to start, naming each flag set
(ADR-034#conflicting-auth-only-env-flags-are-a-boot-error, #4139). Do not
"fix" that by making this line pick a winner.

records.heading: auth: full.sso.sso_display_name

notes: fallback is an empty string, not unset

comment: SSO display name (shown on "Sign in with X" button)
DEPRECATED: Each provider now carries its own display name via
OIDC_DISPLAY_NAME, ENTRA_DISPLAY_NAME, GOOGLE_DISPLAY_NAME, etc.
Retained for backward compatibility with single-provider OIDC setups.

records.heading: auth: full.sso.allow_platform_fallback_for_tenants
comment: Multi-tenant SSO fallback policy
Controls whether custom domains without their own CustomDomain::SsoConfig
can fall back to platform ENV-based SSO credentials.
When true, any custom domain can piggyback on platform SSO — convenient
for single-tenant deployments but a security concern in multi-tenant setups.
When false, custom domains must have explicit per-domain SSO configuration
or SSO will be unavailable on that domain.
Default: false (require explicit per-domain SSO configuration)

records.heading: auth: full.sso.trust_email_for_linking
comment: Email-based account linking trust (deprecated single-OIDC / global default)
The ONE sanctioned exception to the invariant that email may LOCATE an
account but only a demonstrated credential may BIND. When true, an SSO
identity whose email matches an existing account is auto-linked to it,
instead of being refused (the H-3 default). Only enable this when the
operator controls BOTH OTS and the IdP (self-hosted single-tenant, #3836).
This global value applies to the platform (env-configured) provider path
only; it is ignored on the multi-tenant (tenant SsoConfig) surface by
construction. Per-provider overrides (OIDC_TRUST_EMAIL_FOR_LINKING,
ENTRA_TRUST_EMAIL_FOR_LINKING, GOOGLE_*, GITHUB_*, GITLAB_*) take precedence.
Default: false (refuse email-based auto-linking — require explicit,
authenticated linking from account settings)

records.heading: auth: full.argon2_secret
comment: Argon2 secret key (pepper) for password hashing defense-in-depth.
Folded into password hashes — if the hash database is compromised,
passwords remain protected unless this secret is also leaked.
Leave unset (nil) to use argon2id without a pepper.

records.heading: logging: audit.syslog.url
comment: protocol://host:port — 'syslog://localhost' writes to the LOCAL syslog
daemon and needs nothing extra. 'tcp://loghost:514' / 'udp://loghost:514'
ship to a REMOTE syslog server, which SemanticLogger implements with the
third-party `syslog_protocol` gem (plus `net_tcp_client` for tcp://);
neither is bundled here, so a remote URL needs them added to the Gemfile.
Without them the appender is skipped with one warning at boot and the
audit stream still reaches stdout — it is never silently dropped.

records.heading: logging: audit.syslog.facility

records.heading: logging: http.level
comment: Overrides loggers.HTTP level for requests

records.heading: logging: http.capture
comment: Capture mode determines what data is logged per request
Options: minimal, standard, debug
minimal:  method, path, status, duration
standard: + request_id, ip
debug:    + params, headers, session_id

records.heading: logging: http.allowed_error_fields
comment: Opt-in allowlist of request field names (params or header display names,
e.g. "ttl" or "User-Agent") that may appear in request/error logging
beyond the baseline method/path/status/duration/request_id/ip. This is
the one dial for both:
- :debug capture mode's params/headers above (empty = neither shows,
even with LOG_HTTP_CAPTURE=debug)
- what an unhandled exception / error report (Sentry) may attach from
the triggering request — see Onetime::ErrorHandler.safe_request_context
Empty by default: a request that raises an unhandled exception is then
logged with exactly the same fields as any other request (method, path,
status) — the query string and request body are never logged. This
mirrors Django's SafeExceptionReporterFilter stance: filtering is
opt-in per field, not opt-out via a blocklist that can lag behind new
sensitive field names.
Header names must use the canonical capitalized-with-hyphens form (e.g.
"User-Agent", "X-Forwarded-For") — each HTTP_ env key is normalized by
capitalizing the parts between underscores, so an all-caps acronym like
HTTP_CF_IPCOUNTRY normalizes to "Cf-Ipcountry", not "CF-IPCountry". If a
header you add here doesn't seem to match, check the normalized form
rather than what a browser or proxy sends on the wire.
RequestLogger reads this list once at boot (its middleware instance is
long-lived) — a change here takes effect on the next process restart,
not a live config reload. Sentry's error-report context
(Onetime::ErrorHandler.safe_request_context) re-reads it on every call,
so the two surfaces can briefly disagree if you edit this without
restarting.
Never add names like password, secret, token, passphrase, api_key,
access_token, refresh_token, Authorization, or Cookie here.

records.heading: billing: app_identifier
comment: Product Matching Configuration
region: When set, only Stripe products whose region metadata matches this value
will be imported into the plan cache. This enables regional catalog isolation
so NZ and CA deployments sharing the same Stripe account do not overwrite each
other's plans in Redis (the "last writer wins" collision).
Set via JURISDICTION env var; leave unset (or empty) for global/single-region
deployments where all products are visible.
Example: JURISDICTION=NZ → only products with metadata region=NZ are loaded.
match_fields: Reserved for future composite-key matching. Not read at runtime;
regional isolation is driven solely by the region field above.
Used in Stripe metadata['app'] matching
